changes: Round 4 (transitions only): every cut on the 1/15 s pose grid, so the new camera never shows the old pose; the tone pick-up on both sides with the gloves arriving first and his hand rising into the grip, the sleeve going straight off the side of the frame; the captions placed so none covers his face; the left finger abduction glove coming in and going out by the top edge. The beat panels with moved captions (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8) are re-rendered so the storyboard still matches the film.

Round 3 - pronator drift: both arms straight forward and parallel, the hands exactly shoulder-width apart (the kit's 'outstretched' brings each hand 2.5 cm in; here the hand is straight ahead of the shoulder), palms up, the same height (108.2 cm both, difference 0.0 mm; palms 0.0 deg). The foot-end camera is now far back on a long lens (7 deg), so the near hands no longer spread into a V by perspective.

Round 3 - his fist (shoulder abduction, elbow flexion and extension, wrist extension; both sides): a proper closed fist, searched on the meshes: each fingertip curled onto the palm (0.45-0.56 mm), the thumb across the middle bones of the index and middle fingers (0.00 mm), its shaft in front of the index so no ring shows from the thumb side. Measured as contacts (fist-*). The wrist test was solved again on the new fist (the examiner's fingers 0.50 mm on the back of it).

Round 3 - transitions scan: beat 10 (finger flexion) used to cut in on its close shot while his arm still rested, a frame of empty teal; it now opens on a wider side shot (his resting arm and the space the hand rises into) and the camera follows the arm in as it rises and out as it goes down, on both sides. The other flags were hands entering or leaving at the frame edge for a few frames, not sleeves across the lens.

Checked against the full prompt: update(t) no longer keeps any state between calls (the examiner's hand used to remember the last arm angles while his arm moved to or from rest; it now uses the fixed test position), so frames are identical in any render order.
His arm now holds the test position until the examiner's hand has left it (no arm moving under a hand).
Every rustle starts on the exact pose frame of its event (the arm leaving or reaching the mattress), from the same schedule as the picture.

Elbow cup (tone): the hand is now searched for its turn on the elbow as well as where it sits (turned 40 deg), and solved at every pose frame his arm takes while the examiner holds it (149 frames; the arm moves on twos, so nothing is blended between solved poses, which before let the fingers sink up to 15 mm into the elbow). The palm cups the back of the elbow and all four fingers wrap round its inner side; every finger PAD rests on the skin (palm 0.50-0.52 mm, fingers 0.15-0.81 mm, pads 0.49-0.81 mm). No finger joint bends past its limit (before, the little finger was curled past 160 deg at the middle joint).

Pads: every finger and thumb contact is now also measured at its pad (the end bone), not only at its nearest point, and the solver bends a finger's joints until its pad rests on the skin. This found and fixed the handshake (the examiner's middle finger and his middle and ring fingers had pads 4-6 mm off) and the elbow-flexion thumb (3.2 mm). All 96 pads: 0.05-1.09 mm.
Grip: his thumb starts from NEURO.HAND.grip and its two joints are flexed until its pad rests on the gloved fingers: pad 0.05 mm (nearest point 0.00 mm), shown in the side and below panels (e).
Cup panel (b): filmed from above the inner side of the elbow, where the fingers wrap (the old camera was inside the mattress).
checks: Contacts: every contact is measured on the meshes of the rendered frames, at its nearest point and, for fingers and thumbs, at its pad; the tone contacts at every pose frame of the moves, the power tests at mid-press, his own fist at the four tests that use it. All 124 pass (0-1.5 mm).

Hand rules: fingers together in every contact (each finger may turn at most 0.15 rad toward its neighbours to reach the skin), no V (the two gloved fingers of the grip side by side), no upright hand on the bed, no hand on its edge except the pointing hand of finger abduction, whose index comes down onto the side of his finger from above.

His RIGHT and LEFT: checked in the plan panel (a); every left-side test is filmed from his left with the examiner on his left (the sleeves leave the frame on that side); the bedside table is on his left near his head and no camera passes through it or the bed.
No text in the scene: only the caption plaque (off in the review panels, which carry review labels only).
The neck is the kit's slim neck (no change to shared/).

Every sign named in a caption can be seen: inspection shows both shoulders, upper arms, forearms and the backs of both hands; drift shows both palms level and his closed eyes; each power panel shows the named point and the examiner's hand.
assumptions: He stays half-sitting at 45 degrees for the whole part (as the brief allows); 'the upper arm resting on the bed by his side' is the upper arm lying along the backrest beside his trunk.

Wrist extension: with the trunk at 45 degrees his forearm cannot lie flat on the mattress with the elbow bent, so it lies palm down beside him resting on the examiner's other palm, which steadies it from below; the fist is cocked up from there.
Finger flexion: his forearm points forward with the thumb up, so the examiner's two fingers go down through his grip from the thumb side and their tips come out under his little finger.
Finger abduction: his hand rests on the front of his thigh (on the pyjama trousers, 10 cm above the knee).
Each 'hold' is 1.5 s with the picture still apart from his quiet breathing; his only words are 'no' (beat 2), as silent visemes.

The limb gives about 2 mm under the examiner's hand and then holds (shoulder 0.55 deg, elbow 0.6 deg, wrist 1.8 deg, the hand 0.55 deg of elbow, the index finger about 2 mm); the working muscle firms by about 1 mm (no lump). Finger abduction: no firming of the first dorsal interosseous is modelled (it would read as a lump at that size).

The kit's fist leaves a see-through loop seen from the thumb side, so this part uses its own fist (the fingers bent more at the middle joints, the thumb across the front of the index and middle fingers); the kit's NEURO.HAND poses are used for the drift (together), the grip and finger abduction (spread).

Tone moves: the wrist 45 deg flexion to 38 deg extension, the forearm 72 deg supination to 55 deg pronation, the elbow 28 to 112 deg, the shoulder 4 to 30 deg out, at irregular speeds; the left arm 1.3 times faster.

Between beats the view changes by hard cuts that land on him (allowed by the brief's transition rules), and the walk round to his left and back is always a hard cut, as asked; FLOW BETWEEN BEATS' 'no hard cuts' is overridden by MY CONTENT here.
open: The raised arm (outstretched, abduct90): the top of the shoulder reads as the kit's rounded clay joint (v5 limit), see panel f.
Sound: only the room bed and soft rustles, as MY CONTENT asks (no contact sounds or music, which SOUND (no voiceover) would otherwise suggest).
